excerpt: BIT 4484 Notes 7 26 2020 covers project planning essentials.
notes:
Chapter 5 - Planning Projects pt2

Schedule and Cost

Project Planning (Review) - Guides project execution

Project Schedule Management

Schedule management plan - details how the schedule will be managed

Defining Activities

Activity - Distinct, scheduled portion of work performed during a project

Activity List - Tabular list of activities to be included on a project schedule

Defined by identifying activities required to create each work package on the WBS

WBS 100% Rule - Once you complete all the work for the work packages, the project should be done

Date the completion of each work package

Interim Deliverables - Deliverables needed to create the final product, but are discarded after project completion

Ex. Program for internal testing during development

Work packages - Deliverables

Milestone List

Milestone - significant point or event in a project

Generally encompass many completed activities

Should be developed early

Small and frequent

Binary

Completed or missed

Activity - Work

Deliverable - Output

Milestone - Marker for progress

Should be SMART

Specific

Measurable

Attainable

Relevant

Time-framed

Sequencing and Planning

Dependencies

Reason

Mandatory - Inherent within nature of project

Ex. Can’t hold training classes until training materials are ready

Discretionary - Defined by project team

Ex. Don’t start working until project is signed off on

External - Defined by someone outside project team

Ex. Can’t start development until supplies are delivered

Internal - Within team’s control

Ex. Must build a machine before testing it

Type

Finish-to-Start - Task B cannot start until Task A is finished

Most common (90%)

Start-to-Start - Task B cannot start until Task A is started

Finish-to-Finish - Task B cannot finish until Task A is finished

Start-to-Finish - Task B cannot finish until Task A is started

Rarely used

Estimating Resources

Duration Estimating

Duration - Total amount of elapsed time from activity start to finish

Used to determine schedule

Discrete - Exact value estimate

Range estimate

3-point Estimate - Optimistic, most likely, AND pessimistic values for duration



Lead Time - Time you can start an activity before its prerequisite is done

Negative

Lag Time - Time after an activity has been completed before you can start the next one

Positive

Effort - Amount of time spent working to complete a task

Used to determine labor costs

Gantt Charts 

Bar chart based on prerequisites and activity durations





Project Networks

Objective - Minimize project completion time

Uses a network diagram

Activity-on-Arrow Approach

Activities represented by arcs

Can only be used by finish-start dependencies

(kind of suck, won't be explaining)

Activity-on-Node Approach

Also called Precedence Diagramming Method

Activities represented by nodes

Used by PM software





Largest, so duration is 38

Critical Activities - B-D-E-F

Critical Path Method

2 Passes - One forward, one backward









Critical Activities - Those with 0 Slack

No wiggle room before required start and earliest start

1:18:00 (Video)

Critical Path - Shortest time in which project can be completed

Cannot delay any project along path without delaying project

Schedule Compression

Crashing - Making cost and schedule trade-offs to obtain the optimal amount of compression-cost tradeoff

Ex. Pay $1000 to shorten Activity 1 by a week

Fast Tracking - Doing activities in parallel that would normally be done in sequence

Risky, can backfire

Multitasking - One resource works on more than one project at the time time

Delays each individual part

Buffer - Built in extra time to complete a task

Project buffer - Buffer to complete an entire project

Feeding Buffer - Buffer before critical activities on non-critical activities (see lecture)

Parkinson’s Law - Work expands to fit allotted time

Cost Estimates

Analogous Estimates - Estimation by comparing to actual costs of a similar project	

Top-down

Bottom-Up - Estimate the cost of each activity, then adding them all up

Parametric Modeling - Based on estimated costs of materials to complete tasks

Cost Budgeting - Produces a cost baseline

Time-phased budget
